construct: Unlike most anterior-pituitary hormones, prolactin is under dominant tonic inhibitory control from hypothalamic tuberoinfundibular dopamine. Dopamine reaches lactotrophs through portal blood and activates D2 receptors, reducing prolactin synthesis and secretion; dopamine antagonism or pituitary-stalk disruption removes this inhibition and raises prolactin.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: Tuberoinfundibular dopamine tonically suppresses lactotroph prolactin synthesis/secretion through D2 receptors; antagonism removes that inhibition.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: TRH is a real regulator of prolactin but is stimulatory rather than the dominant tonic inhibitory signal specified in the experiment.
adversarial_second_pass.expert_reviewer_reversal: The dopamine-antagonist-sensitive inhibitory effect on lactotrophs uniquely identifies the D2 receptor.
